title: $Rf_!$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$: assembled from $i_!$ and $Rp_*$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)\subseteq D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ for the bounded constructible derived category of module objects over the pulled-back coefficient ring $\Lambda_T$, with its inclusion functor, as defined there. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring
for which the derived pushforwards restrict to bounded constructible complexes
([sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]; for instance $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E,\underline E,\underline{\Qlb}$).
For a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ and a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)$
of $f$, the *lower shriek attached to $c$* is the composite of the two restricted functors of
[sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]:

$$
Rf_!^c:=Rp_*\circ i_!\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda).
$$

The *derived lower shriek* is $Rf_!:=Rf_!^{c_f}$ for the chosen compactification $c_f$ of
[sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. No separate preservation statement is needed for $Rf_!$.

The functor $Rf_!^c$ is compatible with the ambient lower shriek
$Rf_!^c=R(p_*)\circ D(i_!)$ on $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]:
there is a natural isomorphism $\iota\circ Rf_!^c\cong Rf_!^c\circ\iota$, with $\iota$ the inclusions
of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$. In particular $Rf_!$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is compatible with the ambient
$Rf_!$ for the chosen compactification.

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], the compactification $c=(i,p)$ stays inside the setting: $Z$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, $i$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors], $F=i_!$ is a functor from $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ to $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$ for every $\Lambda$, and $G=Rp_*$ is a functor from there to $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$ under the preservation hypothesis on $\Lambda$. Define $Rf_!^c=G\circ F$: on objects it sends $K$ to $G(F(K))$, and on a morphism $u$ it sends $u$ to $G(F(u))$. The identity and composition laws follow by applying those of $F$ and $G$. Thus its values already belong to the required constructible category; no new preservation assertion is used.

source.place: definition, first displayed composite; det-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek-definition.md, defining paragraph

proof.text: Write $I_T$ for the inclusion $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)\hookrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$. The restriction clause of [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] gives natural isomorphisms $a:I_Z\circ F\cong D(i_!)\circ I_X$ and $b:I_Y\circ G\cong R(p_*)\circ I_Z$. At an object $K$, define $\theta_K$ as the composite of $b_{F(K)}$ followed by $R(p_*)(a_K)$. This is invertible, with inverse the composite of $R(p_*)(a_K^{-1})$ followed by $b_{F(K)}^{-1}$. For $u:K\to L$, naturality of $b$ gives $b_{F(L)}\circ I_Y(G(F(u)))=R(p_*)(I_Z(F(u)))\circ b_{F(K)}$, and applying $R(p_*)$ to naturality of $a$ gives $R(p_*)(a_L)\circ R(p_*)(I_Z(F(u)))=R(p_*)(D(i_!)(I_X(u)))\circ R(p_*)(a_K)$. Composing these equations proves naturality of $\theta$. By the definition in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], its target is the ambient $Rf_!^c\circ I_X$. Hence $\theta:I_Y\circ Rf_!^c\cong Rf_!^c\circ I_X$ is the asserted compatibility. This is just composition of the given isomorphisms, not an additional geometric theorem.

Take the chosen compactification $c_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] in the preceding construction and define $Rf_!=Rf_!^{c_f}$. The ambient chosen lower shriek of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] is also defined using that chosen compactification. Substituting $c=c_f$ in $\theta$ therefore gives the asserted compatibility for $Rf_!$. No comparison between different compactifications is required.
